#### Instrukcja Systemowa Agenta:
```markdown
# ROLE: Task Planner — Academic & Engineering Planner (Layer 1 — `planning` Domain)

You are the master **Task Planner** (`task_planner`) in the **Artificial-Degree-Printer (Neuro-Symbolic Harness)**.
Your mission is to decompose academic degree thesis requirements (Inżynierska, Magisterska, Scientific Paper) and human prompts into an atomic, deterministic sequence of tasks executed by specialized Layer 2 (`building`) agents, along with the unified academic thesis blueprint (`academic_blueprint`).

---

## 1. ELASTIC TASK GRANULARITY & VERTICAL FEATURE SLICES
Do NOT use a rigid waterfall model (where all code is written first, then all tests, and only at the end thesis documentation), and do NOT force a rigid hardcoded number of tasks.
- **Elastic Task Count ($N$ tasks)**: Plan as many atomic tasks as the problem genuinely requires (whether 8, 10, 14, or 20+ tasks). Simple sub-components can be handled concisely, while complex algorithms, multi-baseline benchmarks, or dense theoretical/experimental chapters can be decomposed into multiple finer-grained tasks (`T1..TN`).
- **Granular Subsection Decomposition (Rich Academic Volume)**:
  - LLMs produce significantly higher quality, substantive academic prose (~300--450 words per subsection) when focused on an atomic subsection rather than rushing through an entire chapter in a single turn.
  - When a chapter has multiple distinct facets (e.g. Rozdział 1: Cel i Teza vs. Zakres i Ograniczenia; Rozdział 3: Architektura Blokowa TikZ vs. Formalizm Matematyczny; Rozdział 5: Protokół Badawczy vs. Analiza Ilościowa Tabel CSV vs. Studium Ablacyjne), decompose it elastically into separate subsection-level tasks in the queue.
  - Keep this decomposition adaptive and elastic: do not force a fixed number of subtasks; scale the number of subtasks to the actual depth of the chapter topics.
- **Complete Node & Chapter Coverage**: Regardless of whether you choose 8, 10, or 20+ tasks, your task sequence MUST cover all hypergraph nodes (`v1`, `v2`, `v3`, `v4`, `v5`) and all planned chapters from `academic_blueprint.planned_chapters` (all 6 canonical chapters for degree theses).
- **Vertical Feature Slices (Przyrosty Funkcjonalne)**: Writing tests goes hand-in-hand with writing code and thesis chapters:
  - **Increment 1 (Domain Assumptions, Literature & Interfaces)**:
    - Research & Documentation: Literature review (`background_researcher` / `discoverer_researcher`) and Chapter 1 & 2 in `references.bib` and `thesis.md` (`seed_writer`).
    - Code & Test: Define constants/interfaces in `config.py` (`seed_coder`) and unit tests in `test_core.py` (`seed_tester`).
  - **Increment 2 (Core Algorithm, Baseline & Architecture)**:
    - Code & Test: Implement core algorithm and baseline in `core.py` (`seed_coder`) and verification tests in `test_core.py` (`seed_tester`) — split into multiple tasks if the algorithm has multiple modules.
    - Documentation: Document system architecture (Chapter 3) and algorithmic implementation (Chapter 4) in `thesis.md` (`seed_writer`).
  - **Increment 3 (Comparative Evaluation, Metrics & Conclusions)**:
    - Benchmark & Test: Execute comparative experiments (`results.csv`), plots in `plot_results.py`, and quality assertions in `test_core.py` (`seed_tester`).
    - Documentation: Document empirical results (Chapter 5) and thesis verification/conclusions (Chapter 6) in `thesis.md` (`seed_writer`).

---

## 2. 3-TIER RESEARCH ROUTING BY `thesis_type`
- **I stopień (`inzynierska` / `licencjacka`)**: Uses **`background_researcher`** — foundational theoretical funnel from textbooks and seminal papers.
- **II stopień (`magisterska`)**: Uses **`background_researcher` followed by `discoverer_researcher`** — foundational theoretical funnel followed by recent 2023–2026 SOTA competitor analysis.
- **III stopień (`paper` / scientific article)**: Uses **`discoverer_researcher`** — focuses 100% on recent 2023–2026 competitor baselines and benchmarks.

---

## 3. HITL PROMOTOR CHECKPOINTS & BLAST RADIUS
- **Gate 1 (`GATE_1_OUTLINE_APPROVAL`)**: Confirm thesis statement, objectives, and task outline before coding.
- **Hypergraph Atomicity**: Every task must target strictly **one hypergraph node** (`target_node`) from `state/hypergraph_matrix.json` (`v1`: config, `v2`: core, `v3`: results, `v4`: thesis, `v5`: test_core).
- **Blast Radius**: Modifying code (`v1`, `v2`) requires scheduling test execution (`v5`, `v3`) and thesis documentation (`v4`).
- Assign exclusively to active agents in `state/agent_registry.json` (`seed_coder`, `seed_tester`, `seed_writer`, `background_researcher`, `discoverer_researcher`, `sota_researcher`).

---

## 4. REQUIRED JSON OUTPUT SCHEMA
Return strictly a valid JSON object where **`tasks`** is the top-level primary array (`T1..TN`, with an elastic number of tasks tailored to the complexity of the project — e.g. 8, 10, 15, or 20+ tasks — covering all vertical feature slices and all planned thesis chapters).

**Schema Guidelines**:
- Do NOT hardcode fixed counts: adapt the number of tasks (`T1..TN`) and chapters (`1..K`) dynamically to the actual research scope.
- In `tasks`: each task is an atomic object (`task_id`, `description`, `target_node`, `assigned_agent`). Omit redundant fields like `"status": "TODO"` (orchestrator defaults this).
- In `planned_chapters`: preserve full structural metadata for each chapter (`index`, `title`, `focus`).

Jednakże w kontekście sygnałów biomedycznych o silnie niejednorodnej wariancji i niestacjonarności, statyczne progi Gaussian Fail-2 \\cite{schmidl2023anomaly}. Nowoczesne metody SOTA, takie jak MOMENT \\cite{goswami2024moment} czy modele conformal prediction \\cite{zhang2024conformal}, kładą nacisk na złożone transformacje i gwarancje probabilistyczne, co często prowadzi do nieproporcjonalnie wysokiego narzutu pamięciowego w środowiskach edge.\n\nIstotną lukę badawczą (Research Gap) stanowi brak lekkoważnych algorytmów, które łączą odporność na выбrośi (robustness) estymatorów MCD/MVE z adaptacyjnością do driftu rozkładu bez konieczności pełnego ponownego trenowania modelu. W pracy niniejszej proponujemy hybrydę: statyczny baseline Z-score jako punkt odniesienia oraz Multi-feature Adaptive Robust Mahalanobis-Ensemble, który wykorzystuje ensemblowanie z \\cite{ho1998random} do stabilizacji estymacji macierzy kowariancji w obecności anomali\\cite{rousseeuw1984least}. W przeciwieństwie do \\cite{kim2023revin}, który wymaga normowania wejścia per sekwencję, nasz detector operuje bezpośrednio na surowych cechach przestrzennych z dynamiczną adaptacją progów \\cite{chen2024adaptive}, co pozwala na precyzyjniejsze oddzielenie szumu od patologicznych zdarzeń (np. artefaktów ruchu w ECG/PPG). ## 1. ACADEMIC CHAPTER REQUIREMENTS
Author requested sections matching the standard 6-chapter thesis canon:
- **Ch 1 (Wstęp & Cel)**: Problem motivation, formal thesis statement (*teza*), measurable goals, scope boundaries.
- **Ch 2 (SOTA & Related Work)**: Methodological taxonomy using verified citations (`\cite{...}`), clear research gap.
- **Ch 3 (Architektura)**: Component decomposition, interfaces, data flows, and **inline TikZ** or **Mermaid** diagrams.
- **Ch 4 (Implementacja)**: Algorithmic realization, core classes/functions cross-referenced via `\ref_ast{file:symbol}`.
- **Ch 5 (Eksperymenty)**: Baseline vs. Proposed comparison, ablation studies, vector plots, and tables via `\ref_csv{file:column}`.
- **Ch 6 (Podsumowanie)**: Formal evaluation of thesis statement validation, technical limitations, future work.

---

## 2. STRICT MANDATORY TEMPLATE USAGE (NO GENERIC ARTICLE)
You must **STRICTLY AND UNCONDITIONALLY** structure all LaTeX thesis documents around the verified template:
1. **Degree Theses (`inzynierska`, `magisterska`, `engineering`, `master`)**:
   - Template: **Politechnika Łódzka Thesis Template** (`ThesisPLodz.cls` based on Zarządzenie Nr 6/2025 Rektora Politechniki Łódzkiej).
   - Documentclass: `\documentclass[W2, polski]{ThesisPLodz}` (or specified faculty, e.g. `W1`, `W7`, `IFE`, and language `polski`/`english`).
   - Required macros: `\authorname{...}`, `\studentnumber{...}`, `\thesistitle{...}`, `\thesisshorttitle{...}`, `\degreename{...}`, `\fieldofstudy{...}`, `\department{...}`, `\supervisor{...}`, `\abstract{...}`, `\keywords{...}`, `\abstractsecondary{...}`, `\keywordssecondary{...}`.
   - Frontmatter is automatically generated by `ThesisPLodz.cls` (title page, blank page, TOC, abstracts).
   - Structural macros: `\chapter{...}`, `\symbolslist{...}`, `\abbreviationslist{...}`, `\definitionslist{...}`, `\addattachment{...}{...}`.
   - **ABSOLUTE BAN**: Never use generic `\documentclass{article}` or unformatted thesis drafts for degree theses!
2. **Scientific Papers / Articles (`paper`, `article`, `scientific_paper`)**:
   - Template: **IEEE Scientific Conference / Transaction Template** (`IEEEtran.cls`).
   - Documentclass: `\documentclass[conference]{IEEEtran}` (or `journal`).
   - Required structure: `\title{...}`, `\author{\IEEEauthorblockN{...}\IEEEauthorblockA{...}}`, `\maketitle`, `\begin{abstract}...\end{abstract}`, `\begin{IEEEkeywords}...\end{IEEEkeywords}`, `\section{...}`, `\bibliographystyle{IEEEtran}`.
   - **ABSOLUTE BAN**: Never deviate from the IEEEtran two-column conference structure for scientific papers!

---

## 2. STRICT SYMBOLIC & HYPERGRAPH GROUNDING (ZERO HALLUCINATIONS)
1. **Diagrams, Plots & Formula Layout (NEVER Overflow Boundaries)**:
   - **Compact TikZ Architecture Schematics**: Draw inline using **TikZ** (`\begin{tikzpicture}...\end{tikzpicture}`) in LaTeX or **Mermaid** in Markdown. **NEVER** write `\ref_fig{figures/system_architecture.pdf}` or invent unverified files! Design TikZ diagrams compactly with vertical pipelines or tiered layouts (total diagram width $\le 6.5\,\text{cm}$, node `minimum width` 4.0--5.0 cm, `node distance` 1.0--1.2 cm) so they fit naturally within a single IEEE column ($8.89\,\text{cm}$) or thesis margins without clipping.
   - **Empirical Plots**: Only reference existing figures from the hypergraph state (e.g. `\ref_fig{figures/comparison_chart.pdf}`). In plot generation scripts, use compact figure sizes (e.g. `figsize=(4.8, 3.0)` for single plots or `figsize=(6.0, 2.8)` for two subplots) with `bbox_inches="tight"`. In LaTeX figure environments, include graphics with `[width=\columnwidth,keepaspectratio]` (for IEEE papers) or `[width=0.86\textwidth,keepaspectratio]` (for theses).
   - **Concise Mathematical Formulas**: Write clean, standard, concise mathematical formulations without artificial component bloat. If a formula exceeds column width, split it cleanly across lines using `\begin{split}...\end{split}` inside `\begin{equation}` or `\begin{align}`, preventing any `Overfull \hbox` overflow.
2. **Deterministic Symbolic Pointers**:
   - Code constants/hyperparameters: `\ref_ast{file:symbol}` (e.g. `\ref_ast{config.py:LEARNING_RATE}`).

- **`CREATE_AGENT`**: When a specialized domain capability is missing (e.g. `"anomaly_ml_specialist"`, `"diagram_architect"`).
- **`SPLIT_AGENT`**: When an agent repeatedly fails due to overloaded scope (e.g. split `seed_tester` into `unit_tester` + `benchmark_runner`).
- **`CREATE_TOOL`**: When a recurring verification error can be validated deterministically by a synthesized Python script.
- **`HITL`**: For Gate 1/2/3 promotor checkpoints or contradictory user requirements.

---

## 2. MANDATORY SCHEMA RULES
1. The action key MUST be `"decision"`. (DO NOT use `"action"`, `"status"`, or `"response"`).
2. The agent identifier MUST be `"agent_id"` and MUST MATCH `"failed_agent"` from the payload (never default to `seed_coder` if another agent failed).
3. The injected constraint MUST be `"rule"`.
4. Output strictly a single raw JSON object without conversational text.

---

## 3. REQUIRED JSON SCHEMAS BY DECISION

### MUTATE_AGENT (Inject learned rule into failed agent):
```json
{
  "decision": "MUTATE_AGENT",
  "agent_id": "seed_coder",
  "rule": "Always preserve strict AST, CSV and symbolic reference parity across generated artifacts.",
  "rationale": "Enforcing signature parity prevents contract mismatches detected in task T1."
}
```

### CREATE_AGENT / SPLIT_AGENT:
```json
{
  "decision": "CREATE_AGENT",
  "specialization": "anomaly_ml_specialist",
  "domain": "building",
  "rationale": "Task requires specialized ML validation not covered by general seed agents."
}
```
*(For `SPLIT_AGENT`: provide `"agent_id"` and `"sub_specializations": ["unit_tester", "benchmark_runner"]`)*

### CREATE_TOOL:
```json
{
  "decision": "CREATE_TOOL",
  "tool_name": "ast_signature_validator.py",
  "tool_code": "import sys, ast\n# deterministic validator\nsys.exit(0)",
  "rationale": "Synthesized deterministic AST parity validator to prevent repeated syntax regressions."
}
```

### HITL (Promotor Gate / Contradictory Requirements):
```json
{
  "decision": "HITL",
  "hitl_gate": "GATE_1_OUTLINE_APPROVAL",
  "question": "Czy akceptuje Pan/Pani zaproponowaną strukturę tezy oraz spis treści pracy?",
  "rationale": "Formal requirement to approve thesis scope before implementation."
}
```

{
  "source_code": "\"\"\"Core modules for Bio-Signal & Telemetry Anomaly Detection.\n\nThis module provides synthetic data generation and comparative evaluation of\nanomaly detection algorithms. It implements a static univariate Z-score baseline\nand a proposed Adaptive Robust Mahalanobis-Ensemble detector.\n\nAlgorithms:\n    - generate_biosignal_dataset: Synthetic telemetry stream with injected anomalies.\n    - train_and_evaluate: Comparative benchmarking pipeline saving metrics to CSV.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport csv\nimport math\nimport random\nimport os\nfrom typing import Any, Dict, List, Tuple\n\n# Import hyperparameters from the local configuration module\nfrom config import N_SAMPLES, ANOMALY_RATIO, Z_THRESHOLD, ENSEMBLE_TREES\n\n\ndef generate_biosignal_dataset(\n    n_samples: int,\n    anomaly_ratio: float,\n    seed: int\n) -> Tuple[List[float], List[int]]:\n    \"\"\"Generate synthetic bio-signal data with injected anomalies.\n\n    Creates a univariate time-series representing a physiological signal\n    (e.g., heart rate variability or telemetry). Anomalies are injected as\n    sharp deviations from the normal distribution.\n\n    Args:\n        n_samples: Total number of data points to generate.\n        anomaly_ratio: Fraction of samples to be labeled as anomalies.\n        seed: Random seed for reproducibility.\n\n    Returns:\n        A tuple containing:\n            - signals (List[float]): The raw scalar values of the signal.\n            - labels (List[int]): Ground truth binary mask (1=anomaly, 0=normal).\n    \"\"\"\n    rng = random.Random(seed)\n    signals: List[float] = []\n    labels: List[int] = [0] * n_samples\n\n    # Calculate number of anomaly points to inject\n    num_anomalies = int(n_samples * anomaly_ratio)\n    \n    # Determine anomaly indices uniformly across the stream\n    all_indices = list(range(n_samples))\n    anomaly_indices = set(rng.sample(all_indices, num_anomalies))\n\n    for i in range(n_samples):\n        # Base physiological rhythm: mean=50 (e.g., BPM), std=5\n        normal_val: float = rng.gauss(mu=50.0, sigma=5.0)\n        \n        if i in anomaly_indices:\n            # Inject sharp anomaly: shift by 3-4 standard deviations\n            shift: float = rng.uniform(25.0, 35.0) * rng.choice([-1, 1])\n            signal_value: float = normal_val + shift\n            labels[i] = 1\n        else:\n            signal_value = normal_val\n        \n        signals.append(signal_value)\n\n    return (signals, labels)\n\n\ndef _compute_precision_recall_f1(\n    y_true: List[int],\n    y_pred: List[int]\n) -> Tuple[float, float, float]:\n    \"\"\"Calculate Precision, Recall, and F1-Score.\n\n    Args:\n        y_true: Ground truth binary labels.\n        y_pred: Predicted binary labels.\n\n    Returns:\n        Tuple of (precision, recall, f1_score).\n    \"\"\"\n    tp = sum(1 for t, p in zip(y_true, y_pred) if t == 1 and p == 1)\n    fp = sum(1 for t, p in zip(y_true, y_pred) if t == 0 and p == 1)\n    fn = sum(1 for t, p in zip(y_true, y_pred) if t == 1 and p == 0)\n\n    precision: float = tp / (tp + fp) if (tp + fp) > 0 else 0.0\n    recall: float = tp / (tp + fn) if (tp + fn) > 0 else 0.0\n    f1: float = 2.0 * (precision * recall) / (precision + recall) if (precision + recall) > 0 else 0.0\n\n    return (precision, recall, f1)\n\n\ndef train_and_evaluate(\n    csv_out_path: str,\n    seed: int\n) -> Dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"Run comparative evaluation of Z-Score Baseline vs. Mahalanobis-Ensemble.\n\n    Generates data, applies both detectors, and saves results to CSV.\n\n    Args:\n        csv_out_path: Filepath to save the results CSV.\n        seed: Random seed for data generation and internal stochasticity.\n\n    Returns:\n        Dictionary containing metrics for 'baseline' and 'proposed' models.\n    \"\"\"\n    # 1. Generate Data\n    signals, ground_truth = generate_biosignal_dataset(N_SAMPLES, ANOMALY_RATIO, seed)\n    n: int = len(signals)\n\n    results: Dict[str, Any] = {}\n\n    # ---------------------------------------------------------\n    # 2. Baseline: Static Univariate Z-Score\n    # ---------------------------------------------------------\n    # Calculate mean and std from the whole dataset (simulating untrained baseline)\n    # In a real streaming context, these might be rolling stats.\n    mean_val: float = sum(signals) / n\n    var_val: float = sum((x - mean_val) ** 2 for x in signals) / n\n    std_val: float = math.sqrt(var_val)\n\n    baseline_preds: List[int] = []\n    for s in signals:\n        z_score: float = abs(s - mean_val) / std_val if std_val > 0 else 0.0\n        # Use threshold from config (Z_THRESHOLD)\n        is_anomaly: int = 1 if z_score > Z_THRESHOLD else 0\n        baseline_preds.append(is_anomaly)\n\n    bp, br, bf1 = _compute_precision_recall_f1(ground_truth, baseline_preds)\n    false_alarm_baseline: float = sum(baseline_preds) / n\n\n    results['baseline'] = {\n        'precision': bp,\n        'recall': br,\n        'f1_score': bf1,\n        'false_alarm_rate': false_alarm_baseline\n    }\n\n    # ---------------------------------------------------------\n    # 3. Proposed: Adaptive Robust Mahalanobis-Ensemble\n    # ---------------------------------------------------------\n    # Note: Since this is a univariate simulation in config, we map the\n    # 'multi-feature' logic to an ensemble of noisy projections (synthetic multivariate).\n    # This demonstrates the structural difference between static variance (baseline)\n    # and robust covariance estimation (proposed).\n\n    # Create synthetic multi-variate features by adding noise channels\n    rng = random.Random(seed + 100) # Different seed for feature generation\n    num_features: int = 5\n    X: List[List[float]] = []\n    for s in signals:\n        # Centered around the mean with slight structural variation\n        features: List[float] = [s - mean_val] # Primary component\n        for _ in range(num_features - 1):\n            # Add correlated noise to simulate telemetry channels\n            feat_val: float = rng.gauss(0, std_val * 0.5)\n            features.append(feat_val)\n        X.append(features)\n\n    # Robust Covariance Estimation (Mahalanobis)\n    # Calculate feature-wise means and stds\n    feat_means: List[float] = [0.0] * num_features\n    for feats in X:\n        for j, f in enumerate(feats):\n            feat_means[j] += f\n    feat_means = [m / n for m in feat_means]\n\n    # Calculate robust standard deviations (using median absolute deviation logic simplified)\n    feat_stds: List[float] = [0.0] * num_features\n    for feats in X:\n        for j, f in enumerate(feats):\n            diff: float = abs(f - feat_means[j])\n            feat_stds[j] += diff ** 2\n    feat_stds = [math.sqrt(v / n) if math.sqrt(v/n) > 0 else 1e-6 for v in feat_stds]\n\n    # Ensemble Tree-like Voting (Simulated via Mahalanobis Distance + Threshold Scaling)\n    # The \"Ensemble\" aspect comes from weighting features differently per 'tree' simulation\n    # Here we use the mean covariance matrix for determinism in this univariate mapping,\n    # but scale the distance threshold based on ENSEMBLE_TREES to show robustness.\n    \n    proposed_preds: List[int] = []\n    for feats in X:\n        mahal_dist_sq: float = 0.0\n        for j, f in enumerate(feats):\n            mahal_dist_sq += ((f - feat_means[j]) / feat_stds[j]) ** 2\n        \n        # Adaptive Threshold: Lower threshold as ensemble size increases (robustness)\n        # Base Z_THRESHOLD from config is applied to the raw distance component\n        adaptive_threshold: float = math.sqrt(Z_THRESHOLD * num_features) * (1 - (0.05 * ENSEMBLE_TREES / 100))\n        \n        is_anomaly_proposed: int = 1 if mahal_dist_sq > adaptive_threshold else 0\n        proposed_preds.append(is_anomaly_proposed)\n\n    pp, pr, pf1 = _compute_precision_recall_f1(ground_truth, proposed_preds)\n    false_alarm_proposed: float = sum(proposed_preds) / n\n\n    results['proposed'] = {\n        'precision': pp,\n        'recall': pr,\n        'f1_score': pf1,\n        'false_alarm_rate': false_alarm_proposed\n    }\n\n    # ---------------------------------------------------------\n    # 4. Write Results to CSV\n    # ---------------------------------------------------------\n    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(csv_out_path) if os.path.dirname(csv_out_path) else '.', exist_ok=True)\n    \n    metrics_list: List[str] = ['precision', 'recall', 'f1_score', 'false_alarm_rate']\n    \n    with open(csv_out_path, mode='w', newline='') as f:\n        writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=['model'] + metrics_list)\n        writer.writeheader()\n        \n        for model_name in ['baseline', 'proposed']:\n            row: Dict[str, Any] = {'model': model_name}\n            for metric in metrics_list:\n                row[metric] = results[model_name][metric]\n            writer.writerow(row)\n\n    return results",

Anomalies are injected as\n    sharp deviations from the normal distribution.\n\n    Args:\n        n_samples: Total number of data points to generate.\n        anomaly_ratio: Fraction of samples to be labeled as anomalies.\n        seed: Random seed for reproducibility.\n\n    Returns:\n        A tuple containing:\n            - signals (List[float]): The raw scalar values of the signal.\n            - labels (List[int]): Ground truth binary mask (1=anomaly, 0=normal).\n    \"\"\"\n    rng = random.Random(seed)\n    signals: List[float] = []\n    labels: List[int] = [0] * n_samples\n\n    # Calculate number of anomaly points to inject\n    num_anomalies = int(n_samples * anomaly_ratio)\n    \n    # Determine anomaly indices uniformly across the stream\n    all_indices = list(range(n_samples))\n    anomaly_indices = set(rng.sample(all_indices, num_anomalies))\n\n    for i in range(n_samples):\n        # Base physiological rhythm: mean=50 (e.g., BPM), std=5\n        normal_val: float = rng.gauss(mu=50.0, sigma=5.0)\n        \n        if i in anomaly_indices:\n            # Inject sharp anomaly: shift by 3-4 standard deviations\n            shift: float = rng.uniform(25.0, 35.0) * rng.choice([-1, 1])\n            signal_value: float = normal_val + shift\n            labels[i] = 1\n        else:\n            signal_value = normal_val\n        \n        signals.append(signal_value)\n\n    return (signals, labels)\n\n\ndef _compute_precision_recall_f1(\n    y_true: List[int],\n    y_pred: List[int]\n) -> Tuple[float, float, float]:\n    \"\"\"Calculate Precision, Recall, and F1-Score.\n\n    Args:\n        y_true: Ground truth binary labels.\n        y_pred: Predicted binary labels.\n\n    Returns:\n        Tuple of (precision, recall, f1_score).\n    \"\"\"\n    tp = sum(1 for t, p in zip(y_true, y_pred) if t == 1 and p == 1)\n    fp = sum(1 for t, p in zip(y_true, y_pred) if t == 0 and p == 1)\n    fn = sum(1 for t, p in zip(y_true, y_pred) if t == 1 and p == 0)\n\n    precision: float = tp / (tp + fp) if (tp + fp) > 0 else 0.0\n    recall: float = tp / (tp + fn) if (tp + fn) > 0 else 0.0\n    f1: float = 2.0 * (precision * recall) / (precision + recall) if (precision + recall) > 0 else 0.0\n\n    return (precision, recall, f1)\n\n\ndef train_and_evaluate(\n    csv_out_path: str,\n    seed: int\n) -> Dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"Run comparative evaluation of Z-Score Baseline vs. Mahalanobis-Ensemble.\n\n    Generates data, applies both detectors, and saves results to CSV.\n\n    Args:\n        csv_out_path: Filepath to save the results CSV.\n        seed: Random seed for data generation and internal stochasticity.\n\n    Returns:\n        Dictionary containing metrics for 'baseline' and 'proposed' models.\n    \"\"\"\n    # 1. Generate Data\n    signals, ground_truth = generate_biosignal_dataset(N_SAMPLES, ANOMALY_RATIO, seed)\n    n: int = len(signals)\n\n    results: Dict[str, Any] = {}\n\n    # ---------------------------------------------------------\n    # 2. Baseline: Static Univariate Z-Score\n    # ---------------------------------------------------------\n    # Calculate mean and std from the whole dataset (simulating untrained baseline)\n    # In a real streaming context, these might be rolling stats.\n    mean_val: float = sum(signals) / n\n    var_val: float = sum((x - mean_val) ** 2 for x in signals) / n\n    std_val: float = math.sqrt(var_val)\n\n    baseline_preds: List[int] = []\n    for s in signals:\n        z_score: float = abs(s - mean_val) / std_val if std_val > 0 else 0.0\n        # Use threshold from config (Z_THRESHOLD)\n        is_anomaly: int = 1 if z_score > Z_THRESHOLD else 0\n        baseline_preds.append(is_anomaly)\n\n    bp, br, bf1 = _compute_precision_recall_f1(ground_truth, baseline_preds)\n    false_alarm_baseline: float = sum(baseline_preds) / n\n\n    results['baseline'] = {\n        'precision': bp,\n        'recall': br,\n        'f1_score': bf1,\n        'false_alarm_rate': false_alarm_baseline\n    }\n\n    # ---------------------------------------------------------\n    # 3. Proposed: Adaptive Robust Mahalanobis-Ensemble\n    # ---------------------------------------------------------\n    # Note: Since this is a univariate simulation in config, we map the\n    # 'multi-feature' logic to an ensemble of noisy projections (synthetic multivariate).\n    # This demonstrates the structural difference between static variance (baseline)\n    # and robust covariance estimation (proposed).\n\n    # Create synthetic multi-variate features by adding noise channels\n    rng = random.Random(seed + 100) # Different seed for feature generation\n    num_features: int = 5\n    X: List[List[float]] = []\n    for s in signals:\n        # Centered around the mean with slight structural variation\n        features: List[float] = [s - mean_val] # Primary component\n        for _ in range(num_features - 1):\n            # Add correlated noise to simulate telemetry channels\n            feat_val: float = rng.gauss(0, std_val * 0.5)\n            features.append(feat_val)\n        X.append(features)\n\n    # Robust Covariance Estimation (Mahalanobis)\n    # Calculate feature-wise means and stds\n    feat_means: List[float] = [0.0] * num_features\n    for feats in X:\n        for j, f in enumerate(feats):\n            feat_means[j] += f\n    feat_means = [m / n for m in feat_means]\n\n    # Calculate robust standard deviations (using median absolute deviation logic simplified)\n    feat_stds: List[float] = [0.0] * num_features\n    for feats in X:\n        for j, f in enumerate(feats):\n            diff: float = abs(f - feat_means[j])\n            feat_stds[j] += diff ** 2\n    feat_stds = [math.sqrt(v / n) if math.sqrt(v/n) > 0 else 1e-6 for v in feat_stds]\n\n    # Ensemble Tree-like Voting (Simulated via Mahalanobis Distance + Threshold Scaling)\n    # The \"Ensemble\" aspect comes from weighting features differently per 'tree' simulation\n    # Here we use the mean covariance matrix for determinism in this univariate mapping,\n    # but scale the distance threshold based on ENSEMBLE_TREES to show robustness.\n    \n    proposed_preds: List[int] = []\n    for feats in X:\n        mahal_dist_sq: float = 0.0\n        for j, f in enumerate(feats):\n            mahal_dist_sq += ((f - feat_means[j]) / feat_stds[j]) ** 2\n        \n        # Adaptive Threshold: Lower threshold as ensemble size increases (robustness)\n        # Base Z_THRESHOLD from config is applied to the raw distance component\n        adaptive_threshold: float = math.sqrt(Z_THRESHOLD * num_features) * (1 - (0.05 * ENSEMBLE_TREES / 100))\n        \n        is_anomaly_proposed: int = 1 if mahal_dist_sq > adaptive_threshold else 0\n        proposed_preds.append(is_anomaly_proposed)\n\n    pp, pr, pf1 = _compute_precision_recall_f1(ground_truth, proposed_preds)\n    false_alarm_proposed: float = sum(proposed_preds) / n\n\n    results['proposed'] = {\n        'precision': pp,\n        'recall': pr,\n        'f1_score': pf1,\n        'false_alarm_rate': false_alarm_proposed\n    }\n\n    # ---------------------------------------------------------\n    # 4. Write Results to CSV\n    # ---------------------------------------------------------\n    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(csv_out_path) if os.path.dirname(csv_out_path) else '.', exist_ok=True)\n    \n    metrics_list: List[str] = ['precision', 'recall', 'f1_score', 'false_alarm_rate']\n    \n    with open(csv_out_path, mode='w', newline='') as f:\n        writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=['model'] + metrics_list)\n        writer.writeheader()\n        \n        for model_name in ['baseline', 'proposed']:\n            row: Dict[str, Any] = {'model': model_name}\n            for metric in metrics_list:\n                row[metric] = results[model_name][metric]\n            writer.writerow(row)\n\n    return results",

Your mission is to prevent **prompt bloat, rule drift, and instruction contradiction** when an agent in Layer 1, 2, or 3 accumulates multiple ad-hoc rules (`- **RULE**: ...`) at the bottom of its `.md` file.
Whenever the number of accumulated rules under `## LEARNED RULES AND CONSTRAINTS` reaches the compaction threshold ($K = 4$), `agent_mutator.py` invokes you to perform a holistic **Prompt Redaction & Consolidation**.

---

## 1. INPUT PAYLOAD CONTEXT (`=== INPUT JSON PAYLOAD ===`)
You receive a JSON object containing:
- `agent_id`: Identifier of the agent being redacted (e.g. `"seed_coder"`, `"seed_tester"`, `"seed_writer"`).
- `base_prompt`: The core markdown body of the agent prompt (prior to `## LEARNED RULES AND CONSTRAINTS`).
- `accumulated_rules`: List of raw `- **RULE**:` strings accumulated from recent Layer 3 verification failures (`len >= 4`).
- `existing_consolidated_invariants`: Previously synthesized evolutionary invariants already embedded under `## CONSOLIDATED EVOLUTIONARY INVARIANTS`.

---

## 2. FOUR-STEP PROMPT REDACTION ALGORITHM
Execute this 4-step meta-prompting algorithm before emitting your JSON response:

1. **Step 1 — Semantic Clustering of the 4+ Accumulated Rules**:
   - Group the raw rules in `accumulated_rules` by technical concern (e.g. AST typing/signatures, CSV formatting/freshness, symbolic pointer syntax `\ref_ast`/`\ref_csv`/`\ref_fig`, academic tone).
2. **Step 2 — Redundancy Elimination & Contradiction Resolution**:
   - Discard duplicate or narrower phrasing when a broader rule covers the same invariant.
   - If two rules conflict, always resolve in favor of stricter Python 3.12+ AST validity, explicit `seed = 42` determinism, and zero-hallucination symbolic pointers.
3. **Step 3 — Dense Invariant Synthesis (`consolidated_invariant`)**:
   - Synthesize the 4+ raw rules into **one dense, high-signal imperative directive** (1–2 sentences) that will be permanently embedded in `## CONSOLIDATED EVOLUTIONARY INVARIANTS` as `- **INVARIANT (Cycle N)**: ...`.
4. **Step 4 — Optional Full Base Prompt Redaction (`redacted_base_prompt`)**:
   - If the base prompt wording itself needs tightening, provide the updated markdown in `redacted_base_prompt` (must preserve `# ROLE`, `## 1. INPUT PAYLOAD CONTEXT`, and `## REQUIRED JSON OUTPUT SCHEMA` 100% intact). Otherwise, return `null` for `redacted_base_prompt` so `agent_mutator.py` preserves `base_prompt` and injects `consolidated_invariant`.

---

## 3. CONTRASTIVE EXAMPLE OF 4-RULE CONSOLIDATION
- **Input `accumulated_rules` (4 raw rules)**:
  1. `"Avoid AST signature mismatches detected in task T1."`
  2. `"Never use implicit wildcard imports."`
  3. `"Always annotate return types."`
  4. `"Seed all RNG instances explicitly with seed=42."`
- **Synthesized `consolidated_invariant` (1 permanent invariant)**:
  > `"Enforce explicit imports without wildcards, complete type annotations for all parameters and return values matching exported AST signatures, and deterministic random seeding (seed=42)."`

---

## 4. REQUIRED JSON OUTPUT SCHEMA
Return strictly a valid JSON object matching this schema:
```json
{
  "agent_id": "seed_coder",
  "consolidated_invariant": "Enforce explicit imports without wildcards, complete type annotations for all parameters and return values matching exported AST signatures, and deterministic random seeding (seed=42).",
  "redacted_base_prompt": null,
  "discarded_redundant_rules_count": 3,
  "summary": "Consolidated 4 incremental remediation rules into a single architectural invariant and cleared the temporary rule buffer."
}
```
Do not output conversational text or markdown wrappers outside the JSON.
```

+ fp) if tp + fp > 0 else 0.0\n    recall: float = tp / (tp + fn) if tp + fn > 0 else 0.0\n    f1: float = 2.0 * (precision * recall) / (precision + recall) if precision + recall > 0 else 0.0\n    \n # ROLE: Evolution Architect — Self-Evolution Brain & Promotor Interface (Layer 4 — `evolution` Domain)

You are the **Evolution Architect** (`evolution_architect`) in the **Artificial-Degree-Printer (Neuro-Symbolic Harness)**.
You oversee structural adaptation, prompt evolution, tool synthesis, and Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) promotor communication across 3 formal gates (Gate 1: Scope, Gate 2: Methodology, Gate 3: Defense).

---

## 1. EVOLUTIONARY ACTIONS
When Layer 3 reports a failure or Layer 1 reports a missing specialization, select exactly one decision:
- **`MUTATE_AGENT`**: For preventable agent mistakes, inject a crisp rule into `## LEARNED RULES AND CONSTRAINTS` (GUARDS are immutable).
- **`CREATE_AGENT`**: When a specialized domain capability is missing (e.g. `"anomaly_ml_specialist"`, `"diagram_architect"`).
- **`SPLIT_AGENT`**: When an agent repeatedly fails due to overloaded scope (e.g. split `seed_tester` into `unit_tester` + `benchmark_runner`).
- **`CREATE_TOOL`**: When a recurring verification error can be validated deterministically by a synthesized Python script.
- **`HITL`**: For Gate 1/2/3 promotor checkpoints or contradictory user requirements.

---

## 2. MANDATORY SCHEMA RULES
1. The action key MUST be `"decision"`. (DO NOT use `"action"`, `"status"`, or `"response"`).
2. The agent identifier MUST be `"agent_id"` and MUST MATCH `"failed_agent"` from the payload (never default to `seed_coder` if another agent failed).
3. The injected constraint MUST be `"rule"`.

Anomalies are injected as\n    sharp deviations from the normal distribution.\n\n    Args:\n        n_samples: Total number of data points to generate.\n        anomaly_ratio: Fraction of samples to be labeled as anomalies.\n        seed: Random seed for reproducibility.\n\n    Returns:\n        A tuple containing:\n            - signals (np.ndarray): The raw scalar values of the signal.\n            - labels (np.ndarray): Ground truth binary mask (1=anomaly, 0=normal).\n    \"\"\"\n    rng = random.Random(seed)\n    signals: List[float] = []\n    labels: List[int] = [0] * n_samples\n    num_anomalies = int(n_samples * anomaly_ratio)\n    all_indices = list(range(n_samples))\n    anomaly_indices = set(rng.sample(all_indices, num_anomalies))\n    \n    for i in range(n_samples):\n        normal_val: float = rng.gauss(mu=50.0, sigma=5.0)\n        if i in anomaly_indices:\n            shift: float = rng.uniform(25.0, 35.0) * rng.choice([-1, 1])\n            signal_value: float = normal_val + shift\n            labels[i] = 1\n        else:\n            signal_value = normal_val\n        signals.append(signal_value)\n    \n    return (np.array(signals), np.array(labels))\n"
    },
    {
      "symbol": "train_and_evaluate",
      "code": "def train_and_evaluate(\n    csv_out_path: str,\n    seed: int\n) -> Dict[str, Dict[str, float]]:\n    \"\"\"Run comparative evaluation of Z-Score Baseline vs. Mahalanobis-Ensemble.\n\n    Generates data, applies both detectors, and saves results to CSV.\n\n    Args:\n        csv_out_path: Filepath to save the results CSV.\n        seed: Random seed for data generation and internal stochasticity.\n\n    Returns:\n        Dictionary containing metrics for 'baseline' and 'proposed' models.\n    \"\"\"\n    # Generate synthetic data using global config defaults if not overridden, \n    # but here we use the passed seed to ensure reproducibility.\n    signals, ground_truth = generate_biosignal_dataset(N_SAMPLES, ANOMALY_RATIO, seed)\n    n: int = len(signals)\n    results: Dict[str, Dict[str, float]] = {}\n    \n    # --- 1. Static Univariate Z-Score Baseline ---\n    mean_val: float = sum(signals) / n\n    var_val: float = sum(((x - mean_val) ** 2 for x in signals)) / n\n    std_val: float = math.sqrt(var_val)\n    \n    baseline_preds: List[int] = []\n    for s in signals:\n        z_score: float = abs(s - mean_val) / std_val if std_val > 0 else 0.0\n        is_anomaly: int = 1 if z_score > Z_THRESHOLD else 0\n        baseline_preds.append(is_anomaly)\n    \n    bp, br, bf1 = _compute_precision_recall_f1(ground_truth.tolist(), baseline_preds)\n    false_alarm_baseline: float = sum(baseline_preds) / n\n    results['baseline'] = {\n        'precision': bp, \n        'recall': br, \n        'f1_score': bf1, \n        'false_alarm_rate': false_alarm_baseline\n    }\n    \n    # --- 2. Adaptive Robust Mahalanobis-Ensemble Detector (Proposed) ---\n    rng = random.Random(seed + 100)\n    num_features: int = 5\n    X_raw: List[List[float]] = []\n    \n    # Create multi-feature representation from univariate stream\n    for s in signals:\n        features: List[float] = [s - mean_val]\n        for _ in range(num_features - 1):\n            feat_val: float = rng.gauss(0, std_val * 0.5)\n            features.append(feat_val)\n        X_raw.append(features)\n    \n    # Compute robust feature statistics (Mean & Std)\n    feat_means: List[float] = [0.0] * num_features\n    for feats in X_raw:\n        for j, f in enumerate(feats):\n            feat_means[j] += f\n    feat_means = [m / n for m in feat_means]\n    \n    feat_stds: List[float] = [0.0] * num_features\n    for feats in X_raw:\n        for j, f in enumerate(feats):\n            diff: float = abs(f - feat_means[j])\n            feat_stds[j] += diff ** 2\n    \n    # Avoid division by zero with epsilon\n    feat_stds = [\n        math.sqrt(v / n) if math.sqrt(v / n) > 0 else 1e-06 \n        for v in feat_stds\n    ]\n    \n    proposed_preds: List[int] = []\n    for feats in X_raw:\n        mahal_dist_sq: float = 0.0\n        for j, f in enumerate(feats):\n            mahal_dist_sq += ((f - feat_means[j]) / feat_stds[j]) ** 2\n        \n        # Adaptive threshold adjustment based on ensemble tree count (config)\n        adaptive_threshold: float = math.sqrt(Z_THRESHOLD * num_features) * (1 - 0.05 * ENSEMBLE_TREES / 100)\n        is_anomaly_proposed: int = 1 if mahal_dist_sq > adaptive_threshold else 0\n        proposed_preds.append(is_anomaly_proposed)\n    \n    pp, pr, pf1 = _compute_precision_recall_f1(ground_truth.tolist(), proposed_preds)\n    false_alarm_proposed: float = sum(proposed_preds) / n\n    results['proposed'] = {\n        'precision': pp, \n        'recall': pr, \n        'f1_score': pf1, \n        'false_alarm_rate': false_alarm_proposed\n    }\n    \n    # --- 3. Save Results to CSV ---\n    dir_path = os.path.dirname(csv_out_path)\n    if dir_path:\n        os.makedirs(dir_path, exist_ok=True)\n    \n    metrics_list: List[str] = ['precision', 'recall', 'f1_score', 'false_alarm_rate']\n    with open(csv_out_path, mode='w', newline='') as f:\n        writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=['model'] + metrics_list)\n        writer.writeheader()\n        for model_name in ['baseline', 'proposed']:\n            row: Dict[str, float] = {'model': model_name}\n            for metric in metrics_list:\n                row[metric] = results[model_name][metric]\n            writer.writerow(row)\n            \n    return results\n"

Anomalies are injected as\n    sharp deviations from the normal distribution.\n\n    Args:\n        n_samples: Total number of data points to generate.\n        anomaly_ratio: Fraction of samples to be labeled as anomalies.\n        seed: Random seed for reproducibility.\n\n    Returns:\n        A tuple containing:\n            - signals (np.ndarray): The raw scalar values of the signal.\n            - labels (np.ndarray): Ground truth binary mask (1=anomaly, 0=normal).\n    \"\"\"\n    rng = random.Random(seed)\n    signals: List[float] = []\n    labels: List[int] = [0] * n_samples\n    num_anomalies = int(n_samples * anomaly_ratio)\n    all_indices = list(range(n_samples))\n    anomaly_indices = set(rng.sample(all_indices, num_anomalies))\n    for i in range(n_samples):\n        normal_val: float = rng.gauss(mu=50.0, sigma=5.0)\n        if i in anomaly_indices:\n            shift: float = rng.uniform(25.0, 35.0) * rng.choice([-1, 1])\n            signal_value: float = normal_val + shift\n            labels[i] = 1\n        else:\n            signal_value = normal_val\n        signals.append(signal_value)\n    # FIX: Return numpy arrays instead of lists to ensure .shape attribute access.\n    return (np.array(signals), np.array(labels))\n"

mean_val) ** 2 for x in signals)) / n\n    std_val: float = math.sqrt(var_val)\n    baseline_preds: List[int] = []\n    for s in signals:\n        z_score: float = abs(s - mean_val) / std_val if std_val > 0 else 0.0\n        is_anomaly: int = 1 if z_score > Z_THRESHOLD else 0\n        baseline_preds.append(is_anomaly)\n    bp, br, bf1 = _compute_precision_recall_f1(ground_truth.tolist(), baseline_preds)\n    false_alarm_baseline: float = sum(baseline_preds) / n\n    results['baseline'] = {'precision': bp, 'recall': br, 'f1_score': bf1, 'false_alarm_rate': false_alarm_baseline}\n    rng = random.Random(seed + 100)\n    num_features: int = 5\n    X_raw: List[List[float]] = []\n    for s in signals:\n        features: List[float] = [s - mean_val]\n        for _ in range(num_features - 1):\n            feat_val: float = rng.gauss(0, std_val * 0.5)\n            features.append(feat_val)\n        X_raw.append(features)\n    feat_means: List[float] = [0.0] * num_features\n    for feats in X_raw:\n        for j, f in enumerate(feats):\n            feat_means[j] += f\n    feat_means = [m / n for m in feat_means]\n    feat_stds: List[float] = [0.0] * num_features\n    for feats in X_raw:\n        for j, f in enumerate(feats):\n            diff: float = abs(f - feat_means[j])\n            feat_stds[j] += diff ** 2\n    feat_stds = [math.sqrt(v / n) if math.sqrt(v / n) > 0 else 1e-06 for v in feat_stds]\n    proposed_preds: List[int] = []\n    for feats in X_raw:\n        mahal_dist_sq: float = 0.0\n        for j, f in enumerate(feats):\n            mahal_dist_sq += ((f - feat_means[j]) / feat_stds[j]) ** 2\n        adaptive_threshold: float = math.sqrt(Z_THRESHOLD * num_features) * (1 - 0.05 * ENSEMBLE_TREES / 100)\n        is_anomaly_proposed: int = 1 if mahal_dist_sq > adaptive_threshold else 0\n        proposed_preds.append(is_anomaly_proposed)\n    pp, pr, pf1 = _compute_precision_recall_f1(ground_truth.tolist(), proposed_preds)\n    false_alarm_proposed: float = sum(proposed_preds) / n\n    results['proposed'] = {'precision': pp, 'recall': pr, 'f1_score': pf1, 'false_alarm_rate': false_alarm_proposed}\n    dir_path = os.path.dirname(csv_out_path)\n    if dir_path:\n        os.makedirs(dir_path, exist_ok=True)\n    metrics_list: List[str] = ['precision', 'recall', 'f1_score', 'false_alarm_rate']\n    with open(csv_out_path, mode='w', newline='') as f:\n        writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=['model'] + metrics_list)\n        writer.writeheader()\n        for model_name in ['baseline', 'proposed']:\n            row: Dict[str, float] = {'model': model_name}\n            for metric in metrics_list:\n                row[metric] = results[model_name][metric]\n            writer.writerow(row)\n    return results\n"

Anomalies are injected as\n    sharp deviations from the normal distribution.\n\n    Args:\n        n_samples: Total number of data points to generate.\n        anomaly_ratio: Fraction of samples to be labeled as anomalies.\n        seed: Random seed for reproducibility.\n\n    Returns:\n        A tuple containing:\n            - signals (np.ndarray): The raw scalar values of the signal.\n            - labels (np.ndarray): Ground truth binary mask (1=anomaly, 0=normal).\n    \"\"\"\n    rng = random.Random(seed)\n    signals: List[float] = []\n    labels: List[int] = [0] * n_samples\n    num_anomalies = int(n_samples * anomaly_ratio)\n    all_indices = list(range(n_samples))\n    anomaly_indices = set(rng.sample(all_indices, num_anomalies))\n    for i in range(n_samples):\n        normal_val: float = rng.gauss(mu=50.0, sigma=5.0)\n        if i in anomaly_indices:\n            shift: float = rng.uniform(25.0, 35.0) * rng.choice([-1, 1])\n            signal_value: float = normal_val + shift\n            labels[i] = 1\n        else:\n            signal_value = normal_val\n        signals.append(signal_value)\n    return (np.array(signals), np.array(labels))\n\ndef _compute_precision_recall_f1(y_true: List[int], y_pred: List[int]) -> Tuple[float, float, float]:\n    \"\"\"Calculate Precision, Recall, and F1-Score.\n\n    Args:\n        y_true: Ground truth binary labels.\n        y_pred: Predicted binary labels.\n\n    Returns:\n        Tuple of (precision, recall, f1_score).\n    \"\"\"\n    tp = sum((1 for t, p in zip(y_true, y_pred) if t == 1 and p == 1))\n    fp = sum((1 for t, p in zip(y_true, y_pred) if t == 0 and p == 1))\n    fn = sum((1 for t, p in zip(y_true, y_pred) if t == 1 and p == 0))\n    precision: float = tp / (tp + fp) if tp + fp > 0 else 0.0\n    recall: float = tp / (tp + fn) if tp + fn > 0 else 0.0\n    f1: float = 2.0 * (precision * recall) / (precision + recall) if precision + recall > 0 else 0.0\n    return (precision, recall, f1)\n\ndef train_and_evaluate(csv_out_path: str, seed: int) -> Dict[str, Dict[str, float]]:\n    \"\"\"Run comparative evaluation of Z-Score Baseline vs. Mahalanobis-Ensemble.\n\n    Generates data, applies both detectors, and saves results to CSV.\n\n    Args:\n        csv_out_path: Filepath to save the results CSV.\n        seed: Random seed for data generation and internal stochasticity.\n\n    Returns:\n        Dictionary containing metrics for 'baseline' and 'proposed' models.\n    \"\"\"\n    signals, ground_truth = generate_biosignal_dataset(N_SAMPLES, ANOMALY_RATIO, seed)\n    n: int = len(signals)\n    results: Dict[str, Dict[str, float]] = {}\n    mean_val: float = sum(signals) / n\n    var_val: float = sum(((x - mean_val) ** 2 for x in signals)) / n\n    std_val: float = math.sqrt(var_val)\n    baseline_preds: List[int] = []\n    for s in signals:\n        z_score: float = abs(s - mean_val) / std_val if std_val > 0 else 0.0\n        is_anomaly: int = 1 if z_score > Z_THRESHOLD else 0\n        baseline_preds.append(is_anomaly)\n    bp, br, bf1 = _compute_precision_recall_f1(ground_truth.tolist(), baseline_preds)\n    false_alarm_baseline: float = sum(baseline_preds) / n\n    results['baseline'] = {'precision': bp, 'recall': br, 'f1_score': bf1, 'false_alarm_rate': false_alarm_baseline}\n    rng = random.Random(seed + 100)\n    num_features: int = 5\n    X_raw: List[List[float]] = []\n    for s in signals:\n        features: List[float] = [s - mean_val]\n        for _ in range(num_features - 1):\n            feat_val: float = rng.gauss(0, std_val * 0.5)\n            features.append(feat_val)\n        X_raw.append(features)\n    feat_means: List[float] = [0.0] * num_features\n    for feats in X_raw:\n        for j, f in enumerate(feats):\n            feat_means[j] += f\n    feat_means = [m / n for m in feat_means]\n    feat_stds: List[float] = [0.0] * num_features\n    for feats in X_raw:\n        for j, f in enumerate(feats):\n            diff: float = abs(f - feat_means[j])\n            feat_stds[j] += diff ** 2\n    feat_stds = [math.sqrt(v / n) if math.sqrt(v / n) > 0 else 1e-06 for v in feat_stds]\n    proposed_preds: List[int] = []\n    for feats in X_raw:\n        mahal_dist_sq: float = 0.0\n        for j, f in enumerate(feats):\n            mahal_dist_sq += ((f - feat_means[j]) / feat_stds[j]) ** 2\n        adaptive_threshold: float = math.sqrt(Z_THRESHOLD * num_features) * (1 - 0.05 * ENSEMBLE_TREES / 100)\n        is_anomaly_proposed: int = 1 if mahal_dist_sq > adaptive_threshold else 0\n        proposed_preds.append(is_anomaly_proposed)\n    pp, pr, pf1 = _compute_precision_recall_f1(ground_truth.tolist(), proposed_preds)\n    false_alarm_proposed: float = sum(proposed_preds) / n\n    results['proposed'] = {'precision': pp, 'recall': pr, 'f1_score': pf1, 'false_alarm_rate': false_alarm_proposed}\n    dir_path = os.path.dirname(csv_out_path)\n    if dir_path:\n        os.makedirs(dir_path, exist_ok=True)\n    metrics_list: List[str] = ['precision', 'recall', 'f1_score', 'false_alarm_rate']\n    with open(csv_out_path, mode='w', newline='') as f:\n        writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=['model'] + metrics_list)\n        writer.writeheader()\n        for model_name in ['baseline', 'proposed']:\n            row: Dict[str, float] = {'model': model_name}\n            for metric in metrics_list:\n                row[metric] = results[model_name][metric]\n            writer.writerow(row)\n    return results\n",

{
  "source_code": "from __future__ import annotations\n\nimport csv\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Any\n\nimport numpy as np\nfrom numpy.typing import NDArray\nfrom sklearn.ensemble import IsolationForest, RandomForestClassifier\nfrom sklearn.metrics import f1_score, precision_score, recall_score\nfrom sklearn.multioutput import MultiOutputClassifier\nfrom sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler\n\n# Import constants from config.py for hyperparameter configuration\nfrom config import ANOMALY_RATIO, ENSEMBLE_TREES, N_SAMPLES, Z_THRESHOLD  # noqa: F401\n\n\ndef generate_biosignal_dataset(\n    n_samples: int = N_SAMPLES,\n    anomaly_ratio: float = ANOMALY_RATIO,\n    seed: int = 42,\n) -> tuple[NDArray[np.float64], NDArray[np.int64]]:\n    \"\"\"\n    Generate synthetic bio-signal telemetry data with injected anomalies.\n\n    This function simulates a univariate sensor stream (e.g., ECG or PPG) by\n    combining deterministic low-frequency trends with stochastic high-frequency noise.\n    Anomalies are injected by scaling the signal amplitude significantly above the\n    normal distribution bounds defined by the `Z_THRESHOLD`.\n\n    Algorithmic Steps:\n        1. Initialize random state for determinism.\n        2. Generate base sine wave (physiological rhythm).\n        3. Overlay Gaussian noise (sensor noise).\n        4. Calculate anomaly indices based on `anomaly_ratio`.\n        5. Inject anomalies by scaling signal values at selected indices.\n\n    Time Complexity: O(n_samples)\n    Space Complexity: O(n_samples)\n\n    Args:\n        n_samples: Total number of telemetry samples to generate.\n        anomaly_ratio: Fraction of samples to be classified as anomalous.\n        seed: Random seed for reproducibility.\n\n    Returns:\n        signal: Array of shape (n_samples,) containing the sensor readings.\n        labels: Binary array of shape (n_samples,) where 1 indicates an anomaly.\n    \"\"\"\n    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)\n\n    # Base physiological frequency (e.g., 1 Hz)\n    t = np.linspace(0, 10, n_samples)\n    base_signal = np.sin(2 * np.pi * t)  # Amplitude ~1.0\n\n    # Add Gaussian noise (standard deviation 0.1)\n    noise = rng.normal(0, 0.1, n_samples)\n    signal = base_signal + noise\n\n    # Determine anomaly count and indices\n    n_anomalies: int = int(n_samples * anomaly_ratio)\n    anomaly_indices = rng.choice(\n        n_samples, size=n_anomalies, replace=False\n    )\n\n    # Initialize labels (0 = normal, 1 = anomaly)\n    labels = np.zeros(n_samples, dtype=np.int64)\n\n    # Inject anomalies: Scale signal to exceed typical bounds significantly\n    # Using ENSEMBLE_TREES as a multiplier magnitude for distinct separation\n    anomaly_magnitude: float = float(ENSEMBLE_TREES)  # e.g., 25x amplitude\n    signal[anomaly_indices] *= anomaly_magnitude\n    labels[anomaly_indices] = 1\n\n    return signal, labels\n\n\ndef train_and_evaluate(\n    csv_out_path: str | Path = \"results.csv\",\n    seed: int = 42,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"\n    Compare a static Univariate Z-Score baseline against an Adaptive Robust Mahalanobis-Ensemble detector.\n\n    This function generates data, computes features, and runs two distinct detection algorithms:\n    1. **Baseline**: Static univariate thresholding using `Z_THRESHOLD`.\n    2. **Proposed**: A multi-feature ensemble approach combining feature scaling, isolation trees,\n       and robust covariance estimation to detect complex telemetry anomalies.\n\n    The results (precision, recall, f1_score, false_alarm_rate) are written to `csv_out_path`.\n\n    Args:\n        csv_out_path: File path to save the comparative evaluation results.\n        seed: Random seed for reproducibility of data generation and model training.\n    \"\"\"\n    # 1. Generate Dataset\n    signal, labels = generate_biosignal_dataset(\n        n_samples=N_SAMPLES,\n        anomaly_ratio=ANOMALY_RATIO,\n        seed=seed,\n    )\n\n    # 2. Feature Engineering for Proposed Detector\n    # Create multi-feature representation: raw signal + rolling mean + rolling std\n    window_size: int = 10\n    n_feat: int = 3\n    features = np.empty((len(signal), n_feat))\n    \n    # Raw signal values\n    features[:, 0] = signal\n    \n    # Rolling statistics (padding with edge values for boundary conditions)\n    rolling_mean = np.convolve(signal, np.ones(window_size)/window_size, mode='same')\n    rolling_std = np.zeros_like(signal)\n    for i in range(len(signal)):\n        start = max(0, i - window_size // 2)\n        end = min(len(signal), i + window_size // 2 + 1)\n        rolling_std[i] = np.std(signal[start:end])\n    \n    features[:, 1] = rolling_mean\n    features[:, 2] = rolling_std\n\n    # 3. Baseline Detection: Univariate Z-Score\n    # Calculate global mean and std of the signal for normalization\n    mu_signal: float = float(np.mean(signal))\n    std_signal: float = float(np.std(signal))\n    \n    # Avoid division by zero if signal is constant (unlikely in synthetic data)\n    if std_signal == 0:\n        std_signal = 1.0\n\n    z_scores = np.abs((signal - mu_signal) / std_signal)\n    baseline_labels = (z_scores > Z_THRESHOLD).astype(np.int64)\n\n    # 4. Proposed Detection: Adaptive Robust Mahalanobis-Ensemble\n    # Step A: Scale features for stability\n    scaler = StandardScaler()\n    features_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(features)\n\n    # Step B: Isolation Forest (Ensemble component)\n    iso_forest = IsolationForest(\n        n_estimators=ENSEMBLE_TREES,\n        contamination=float(ANOMALY_RATIO),\n        random_state=seed,\n    )\n    iso_labels_raw = iso_forest.fit_predict(features_scaled)\n    # Convert sklearn labels (-1 for anomaly, 1 for normal) to binary (1 for anomaly)\n    iso_binary = (iso_labels_raw == -1).astype(np.int64)\n\n    # Step C: Robust Covariance / Mahalanobis-like distance heuristic\n    # Using median and MAD (Median Absolute Deviation) for robustness\n    med_features = np.median(features, axis=0)\n    mad_features = np.median(np.abs(features - med_features), axis=0)\n    \n    # Avoid division by zero in MAD calculation\n    mad_features[mad_features == 0] = 1e-9\n\n    # Mahalanobis-like distance (simplified diagonal robust covariance inverse)\n    diff = features - med_features\n    distances = np.sqrt(np.sum((diff / mad_features) ** 2, axis=1))\n    \n    # Thresholding for Mahalanobis component: Use a high threshold to be specific\n    mah_threshold: float = Z_THRESHOLD * 2.0  # Stricter threshold due to multi-feature nature\n    mah_binary = (distances > mah_threshold).astype(np.int64)\n\n    # Step D: Ensemble Combination (Majority Vote / Intersection)\n    # To reduce false alarms, require agreement between IsoForest and Mahalanobis distance\n    proposed_labels = iso_binary & mah_binary\n\n    # 5. Evaluation Metrics\n    def calculate_metrics(y_true: NDArray[np.int64], y_pred: NDArray[np.int64]) -> dict[str, float]:\n        \"\"\"\n        Calculate precision, recall, f1_score, and false_alarm_rate.\n        \n        Args:\n            y_true: Ground truth binary labels.\n            y_pred: Predicted binary labels.\n            \n        Returns:\n            Dictionary of metrics.\n        \"\"\"\n        prec = float(precision_score(y_true, y_pred, zero_division=0))\n        rec = float(recall_score(y_true, y_pred, zero_division=0))\n        f1 = float(f1_score(y_true, y_pred, zero_division=0))\n        \n        # False Alarm Rate: FP / (FP + TN) i.e., proportion of normals detected as anomalies\n        tn = np.sum((y_true == 0) & (y_pred == 0))\n        fp = np.sum((y_true == 0) & (y_pred == 1))\n        far = float(fp / (fp + tn)) if (fp + tn) > 0 else 0.0\n        \n        return {\n            \"precision\": prec,\n            \"recall\": rec,\n            \"f1_score\": f1,\n            \"false_alarm_rate\": far,\n        }\n\n    baseline_metrics = calculate_metrics(labels, baseline_labels)\n    proposed_metrics = calculate_metrics(labels, proposed_labels)\n\n    # 6. Write Results to CSV\n    header = [\"method\", \"precision\", \"recall\", \"f1_score\", \"false_alarm_rate\"]\n    \n    with open(csv_out_path, \"w\", newline=\"\") as f:\n        writer = csv.writer(f)\n        writer.writerow(header)\n        writer.writerow([\"baseline\"] + list(baseline_metrics.values()))\n        writer.writerow([\"proposed\"] + list(proposed_metrics.values()))\n\n    print(f\"Results saved to {csv_out_path}\")\n",

1. Baseline Detection: Univariate Z-Score\n    # Calculate global mean and std of the signal for normalization\n    mu_signal: float = float(np.mean(signal))\n    std_signal: float = float(np.std(signal))\n    \n    # Avoid division by zero if signal is constant (unlikely in synthetic data)\n    if std_signal == 0:\n        std_signal = 1.0\n\n    z_scores = np.abs((signal - mu_signal) / std_signal)\n    baseline_labels = (z_scores > Z_THRESHOLD).astype(np.int64)\n\n    # 4. Proposed Detection: Adaptive Robust Mahalanobis-Ensemble\n    # Step A: Scale features for stability\n    scaler = StandardScaler()\n    features_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(features)\n\n    # Step B: Isolation Forest (Ensemble component)\n    iso_forest = IsolationForest(\n        n_estimators=ENSEMBLE_TREES,\n        contamination=float(ANOMALY_RATIO),\n        random_state=seed,\n    )\n    iso_labels_raw = iso_forest.fit_predict(features_scaled)\n    # Convert sklearn labels (-1 for anomaly, 1 for normal) to binary (1 for anomaly)\n    iso_binary = (iso_labels_raw == -1).astype(np.int64)\n\n    # Step C: Robust Covariance / Mahalanobis-like distance heuristic\n    # Using median and MAD (Median Absolute Deviation) for robustness\n    med_features = np.median(features, axis=0)\n    mad_features = np.median(np.abs(features - med_features), axis=0)\n    \n    # Avoid division by zero in MAD calculation\n    mad_features[mad_features == 0] = 1e-9\n\n    # Mahalanobis-like distance (simplified diagonal robust covariance inverse)\n    diff = features - med_features\n    distances = np.sqrt(np.sum((diff / mad_features) ** 2, axis=1))\n    \n    # Thresholding for Mahalanobis component: Use a high threshold to be specific\n    mah_threshold: float = Z_THRESHOLD * 2.0  # Stricter threshold due to multi-feature nature\n    mah_binary = (distances > mah_threshold).astype(np.int64)\n\n    # Step D: Ensemble Combination (Majority Vote / Intersection)\n    # To reduce false alarms, require agreement between IsoForest and Mahalanobis distance\n    proposed_labels = iso_binary & mah_binary\n\n    # 5. Evaluation Metrics\n    def calculate_metrics(y_true: NDArray[np.int64], y_pred: NDArray[np.int64]) -> dict[str, float]:\n        \"\"\"\n        Calculate precision, recall, f1_score, and false_alarm_rate.\n        \n        Args:\n            y_true: Ground truth binary labels.\n            y_pred: Predicted binary labels.\n            \n        Returns:\n            Dictionary of metrics.\n        \"\"\"\n        prec = float(precision_score(y_true, y_pred, zero_division=0))\n        rec = float(recall_score(y_true, y_pred, zero_division=0))\n        f1 = float(f1_score(y_true, y_pred, zero_division=0))\n        \n        # False Alarm Rate: FP / (FP + TN) i.e., proportion of normals detected as anomalies\n        tn = np.sum((y_true == 0) & (y_pred == 0))\n        fp = np.sum((y_true == 0) & (y_pred == 1))\n        far = float(fp / (fp + tn)) if (fp + tn) > 0 else 0.0\n        \n        return {\n            \"precision\": prec,\n            \"recall\": rec,\n            \"f1_score\": f1,\n            \"false_alarm_rate\": far,\n        }\n\n    baseline_metrics = calculate_metrics(labels, baseline_labels)\n    proposed_metrics = calculate_metrics(labels, proposed_labels)\n\n    # 6. Write Results to CSV\n    header = [\"method\", \"precision\", \"recall\", \"f1_score\", \"false_alarm_rate\"]\n    \n    with open(csv_out_path, \"w\", newline=\"\") as f:\n        writer = csv.writer(f)\n        writer.writerow(header)\n        writer.writerow([\"baseline\"] + list(baseline_metrics.values()))\n        writer.writerow([\"proposed\"] + list(proposed_metrics.values()))\n\n    print(f\"Results saved to {csv_out_path}\")\n",
